gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 concerns nonconvex sphere-constrained AO subproblems and the applicability of a convergence theorem. It does not recognize the distinct failure that a purported polynomial-time reduction lacks rational target encoding, polynomial bit-size bounds, and a polynomial construction after spectral normalization and Cholesky factorization.

ISSUE-001 discusses the different implication that stationarity or blockwise optimality need not imply local minimality, with a simultaneous-rotation example. It does not identify the gold defect: the unsupported claim that every local minimum is Nash without the nonpositive-objective sign condition, nor the positive-valued local-minimum counterexample.

ISSUE-002 recognizes nonconvexity of sphere intersections and an unsupported AO convergence argument. It does not recognize the separate algebraic defect that an arbitrary, non-orthonormal basis is incorrectly treated as producing the orthogonal projector VV^T, nor the resulting false feasibility equivalence.

ISSUE-003 concerns extrapolated simplex updates that can leave the feasible simplex. It does not address the distinct spectral-norm identity failure caused by using arbitrary scaled bases instead of orthonormal bases in the compressed matrix formula.

Both entries identify that the actual unit-sphere block subproblems are nonconvex, so the cited convex-block AO convergence justification does not apply. ISSUE-002 also explicitly distinguishes the preceding unit-ball relaxation from the equality-constrained updates and requires a repair applicable to the actual sphere problems or withdrawal of the guarantee.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The claimed subsequential critical-pair convergence guarantee is unsupported because the displayed and implemented AO block feasible sets impose norm equality and are nonconvex, contrary to the convex-block premise invoked for the theorem.
